## What changed

**The long waits now say what they are doing and how far along they are.**
Predownload pulls nineteen packages of a gigabyte each through a proxy; the
screen said `предзагрузка пакетов идёт` and then nothing at all, sometimes for
hours. Installation was the same: download, unpack and reconfigure, silent
throughout. A person watching that cannot tell a working upgrade from a hung
one, which is the whole reason they are watching.

apt has a machine-readable progress channel (`APT::Status-Fd`), and it is now
read as it arrives rather than collected at the end:

```
предзагрузка пакетов  3/19 · gitlab-ee amd64 14.9.5-ee.0 · 1 093 MB · 78%
загружен 14.9.5-ee.0 · 6 мин
установка пакета      14.9.5-ee.0 · Running dpkg · 40%
```

The step number is announced *before* its download starts, not after it
finishes — "running" with no indication of what is running is what made this
indistinguishable from a hang in the first place.

Repeated percentages are dropped: apt emits the same value dozens of times a
second, and forwarding all of them would redraw the screen for nothing and
bloat the journal. The line formats were taken from live apt output, not from
documentation, and a test holds them: if apt changes them, it fails here rather
than on someone's server mid-climb.

Underneath, `exec` learned to deliver output line by line while a command runs.
It only did so at the end before, which is why nothing could be shown.
